name: Right to be Caymanian -- Children/Grandchildren of Caymanians

qualifying_event.description: A child or grandchild of a Caymanian, aged 18 or over, may apply to the Caymanian Status and Permanent Residency Board for the right to be Caymanian (Immigration (Transition) Act, Section 28(2)).
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Birth certificates establishing the parent/grandparent relationship to a Caymanian; proof of the parent's/grandparent's Caymanian status.

requirements.blocker_text: Must be the child or grandchild of a Caymanian, and at least 18 years old. No minimum residency period is specified for this ground.

evidence_required.document: Parent's/grandparent's birth certificate and proof of Caymanian status
3 character references from Caymanians (per Board consideration factors, Section 30)

sources.title: Cayman Islands Immigration (Transition) Act (2022 Revision) -- Section 28(2): the right to be Caymanian for children/grandchildren of Caymanians aged 18+; Section 30: Board consideration factors (public interest, character references, criminal record, health, economic impact)

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of the Cayman Islands' initial build. Cayman is the third British Overseas Territory (BOT) built this session, after Anguilla and Montserrat, and the same key modelling decision applies and is explained once here: 'the right to be Caymanian' (also called Caymanian status) is the Cayman Islands' own local legal status -- akin to Belonger status in Anguilla and Montserrat -- NOT British nationality. Formal British Overseas Territories Citizenship (BOTC) is a wholly separate track administered via the Office of the Deputy Governor's online portal (see ky_naturalisation_botc.json). leads_to_citizenship is therefore false here, even though a descent-based route leads directly to citizenship in every non-BOT country built this session. Unusually among the BOTs built this session, the Act does specify a Cabinet cap: only 4 discretionary Caymanian-status grants are permitted per calendar year under Section 26(5) (a different, narrower ground than this one, not modelled as its own route) -- flagged here since it shows the overall system is capacity-constrained even though this specific descent ground is not itself capped. Board consideration factors under Section 30 (public interest, dependant numbers, 3 Caymanian character references, criminal record, health, political conduct, economic impact/balance) apply generally across most 'right to be Caymanian' grounds and are listed here as evidence, though the Act frames them as discretionary Board factors rather than a strict pass/fail checklist.
